## Shared infrastructure — `@keenmate/web-components-devkit` (read before touching examples/build files)

This repo follows the Keenmate component standard: the BlissFramework rulebook
(`C:\Git\BlissFramework\guidelines\web-components\` — structure, naming, CSS,
theming, README, CEM, publish) plus the devkit (`../web-components`, published
as `@keenmate/web-components-devkit`), which owns the example-site kit, the
Vite/Playwright configs and the deploy files. Do not re-create or patch those
locally — every local fork is how they drifted apart.

- **Never add** `examples-chapter-nav.js`, `examples-copy-link.js`,
  `examples-controls-store.js`, `examples-shared.css`, `plausible-snippet.html`
  or `scripts/check-variable-manifest.mjs`. The chapter nav, copy-link buttons,
  shared styles, theme switch, version badge and analytics are injected into
  every root `*.html` page by the Vite plugin automatically.
- **Generated — do not edit:** `Dockerfile`, `nginx.conf`, `Makefile`,
  `.dockerignore` (they start with a `GENERATED by kmwc sync` header). Change
  `package.json#kmwc` and run `npx kmwc sync`, or fix the template in the devkit.
  Repo-specific make targets go in `Makefile.local`.
- **Per-component settings** (title, tagline, CSS prefix, ports, accent colours,
  analytics id, image name, canonical origin) live **only** in `package.json#kmwc`.
- **Example page styles:** shared rules are in `@layer kmwc` and read
  `--base-*` tokens (pages support light / dark / auto via the theme switch), so
  any unlayered rule wins. Put component-only rules in `examples-local.css`.
  Re-theme with `kmwc.theme.accentColor`, never by copying CSS. Native form
  controls (inputs, selects, checkboxes, radios, `role="switch"`, buttons) and
  tables are already styled by the kit (`.reference-table`, `.table-striped`,
  `.table-compact`, …; on a phone a `.reference-table` stacks into cards,
  `.table-scroll` keeps it a grid) — don't restyle them per page; `kmwc-native` opts an
  element out. Log lines take the kit tones (`.log-line--ok|info|warn|err|muted`,
  `--action`, timeline cells `.log-line__time` …) — don't colour them per page;
  write event-log lines with `appendLogLine(panel, { name, detail, variant })`
  from `@keenmate/web-components-devkit/examples`, never an `innerHTML` template.
  `<kbd>`, `<mark>`, field widths (`.w-xs` … `.w-lg`) and `.push-end` are kit
  too — no inline styles for them. Page colours come from the kit's `--kmwc-*`
  tokens or `light-dark()` — a literal doesn't follow dark mode (doctor warns);
  a demo that shows fixed colours on purpose goes in `<style data-kmwc-fixed-colors>`
  (one rule: a `/* kmwc-fixed-colors: why */` comment before it; an element's own
  `style="…"`: the attribute on the element).
  If a second component needs a pattern, it belongs in the devkit.
- **Example pages are fragments:** no `<html>`/`<head>`/`<header>` — start with
  `<meta name="kmwc:title" content="…">`, the devkit layout adds the rest. Shared text
  goes in `partials/` via `<kmwc-include>`; show code with `<kmwc-demo>` (the live
  markup IS the snippet) — never hand-copy a demo into a `.code-block`. Its code
  is highlighted at build time; a hand-written `.code-block` gets the same with
  `data-language="svelte"` (html, js, ts, css, json, sh) — no highlighter on the page.
- **Every example has a permanent code:** each `<h2>` starts `TH07 · Title`
  (page prefix + number; a plain `Summary` is exempt). New examples take the
  next free number; never renumber or reuse one — the rules are the rulebook's
  `example-pages.md`.
- **Controls persistence:**
  `import { attachControlsPersistence } from '@keenmate/web-components-devkit/examples'`.
  **Landing page:** `renderExamplesIndex({ pages })` from the same module.
- **Found a bug in a shared helper?** Fix it in `../web-components` (so every
  component gets it), not here. Say so in your summary if you can't.
- **Never ship AI-assistant files:** `package.json` `files` must keep
  `"!**/CLAUDE.md"` and `"!**/.claude"` (a `CLAUDE.md` you add under `src/` is
  otherwise published with it).
- Before finishing: `npx kmwc doctor` must pass — it runs the devkit checks,
  checks the `npm pack` file list for dev-only files, and runs the rulebook's
  `*.checks.sh` suites. A rulebook failure that is a real architectural decision
  goes into `VALIDATION-NOTES.md` under a `## C-XX-N — …` heading (deferrals
  don't count). After changing a page, `npx kmwc check-pages` loads every page at
  desktop and phone widths and reports errors, horizontal overflow and page CSS
  that only matches inside a shadow root (markup a render callback draws there is
  out of page CSS's reach — style it through the component's styles hook).

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## Status

v1 is implemented (milestones M0–M8 of `IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md`). The plan remains the design
spec and records the intent behind the behaviour; `docs/usage.md` is the public API reference.

## Commands

A `Makefile` (generated by `kmwc sync`; repo targets in `Makefile.local`) wraps these (run `make`
for the list). It also has `make kill-port`, `make publish-dry`, `make publish-rc` (the `rc`
dist-tag) and `make publish` (`latest`), plus `make image-build` / `image-run` (examples site on
nginx, port 12410; see BUILD.md). Don't run the publish targets unless the user asks.

- `npm run dev` — Vite dev server on port **12400** (`index.html` hub + `examples-*.html`; ports come from `package.json#kmwc`)
- `npm run build` — `cem analyze` → Vite library build into `dist/` → `check:vars:strict`
- `npm run build:examples` / `preview:examples` — the static examples site in `dist-examples/` (served on 12401)
- `npm run test:unit` — vitest (happy-dom), specs in `test/unit/`. Single file: `npx vitest run test/unit/palette.test.ts`; by name: `npx vitest run -t "context search"`
- `npm run test:e2e` — Playwright against the dev server (reused if running); specs in `e2e/`, one fixture page per spec `test/<area>.html` (shared pieces in `test/fixture-common.js`); import `test`/`expect` from `e2e/fixtures.ts` (pageerror guard); coverage in `test/COVERAGE.md`, findings in `test/NOTES.md`. Single spec: `npx playwright test e2e/wizard.spec.ts`. `e2e/mobile.spec.ts` runs only in the `mobile` (Pixel 7) project
- `npm run check:vars` — `kmwc check-vars`: validate `component-variables.manifest.json` against the built bundle (the shadow CSS is inlined there), in `consumed` mode

## Architecture

`<web-command-palette>` is a framework-agnostic web component. It owns the whole command-palette
state machine and talks to hosts only through properties, events (`open`, `close`, `select`,
`action`, `ready` + camelCase `on*` twins that receive the detail), single-ctx callbacks
(`searchCallback`, `getStepOptionsCallback`, `before{Action,Select}Callback`) and `el.controller`
(the public facade). It follows the Keenmate interaction model (web-components-core `/actions`):
a command is a core `ActionItem` and running one goes through `runAction`
(`beforeActionCallback` → `onClick` → `action` event). It replaces three drifting implementations (pure-admin
vanilla, svelte-pure-admin, keen-pure-admin LiveComponent). **Top design priority: easy to
configure** — `commands` + `searchCallback` must be a complete setup.

- `src/palette.ts` — `CommandPaletteEngine`, DOM-free. Owns modes (`idle`, `command-list`,
  `command-step`, `context-list`, `context-search`, `global-search`), input routing, the wizard,
  filtering, debounced/abortable provider calls and client-side pagination. Exposes read-only
  view state (`items`, `activeIndex`, `listVersion`, `input`, `lockedLength`, …) and reports
  terminal outcomes through `host.effect()`. Unit-tested directly via `test/unit/helpers.ts`.
  PUBLIC (rulebook C-CA-37 / C-CA-39, docs/usage.md "Build your own UI"): `new CommandPaletteEngine(host,
  options)` — `host` = hooks only (`changed`, `effect`, `context`, `element`, `error`); `options` = the settings +
  data under the element's input names (`commands`, `labels`, `searchDebounce`, …), `setOptions(partial)` /
  `getOptions()`; the element passes its values through `setOptions` from `reinit()` / `update()`; the engine owns the one labels resolver (`engine.labels`, core
  `createLabels`) the renderer reads too. No icon / loader options (it draws nothing).
- `src/render.ts` — builds the shadow DOM once (`createShell`) and patches it (`Renderer`). Results
  are rebuilt only when `listVersion`/list state changes; moving the active row only toggles a
  class. Markup must match pure-admin-core's `snippets/command-palette.html`.
- `src/keyboard.ts` — `bindGlobalKeys()` (Ctrl/⌘+K, `g <letter>` sequences over core `/actions`
  `bindShortcuts`) and the input keydown map (`matchesShortcut('Mod+<key>')`).
- `src/web-component.ts` — thin `BlissElement` subclass: the `static inputs` / `static events`
  tables (CEM metadata is generated from them), the engine host (hooks) + `#engineOptions()` (inputs → engine options) (incl. `context()` = `withContext`, so engine-built ctxs carry
  `controller` / `element` / presentation), `createController()` (facade from a method list), overlay/scroll-lock,
  presentation (phone fullscreen sheet), focus. Only the first connected instance owns the global keys.
- `src/usage.ts` — `UsageStore`: favorites + recents (frecency-ranked, pruned to 50 non-favorites),
  persisted via `localStorage` (`usage-key`) or the host's `loadUsageCallback`/`saveUsageCallback`.
  The machine records uses (instant commands, completed runs + answers, contexts, results) and
  offers a run's remembered answers when it's replayed (`#replay`; Enter = `commit()` fast-forwards,
  Tab = `select()` one step).
- `src/filter.ts`, `src/icons.ts`, `src/types.ts` — substring filtering, icon rendering, public types.

### Example pages

The pages use the devkit examples kit (see the block at the top). `index.html` calls
`renderExamplesIndex({ pages })` with the page registry. Each `examples-<feature>.html` is a
fragment: `kmwc:*` meta tags, then `.card` sections with numbered `<h2>`s (each one a chapter),
using only the kit's page classes — the theming gallery's `<style>` is the one exception, because
those rules are the example. Controls sit in `.controls` and are saved with
`attachControlsPersistence('<page-key>')`. Shared demo data is in `examples-data.js`.
`e2e/examples.spec.ts` checks the hub registry and every page.

### CSS pipeline (non-obvious)

Plain CSS, multiselect-style: `src/css/main.css` imports the files into three layers —
`variables` (`variables.css`: every `--cp-*` knob on `:host`, each `var(--base-*, <fallback>)`),
`component` (base, dialog, search, results, footer, badges, confirm, animations) and `overrides`
(`dark-mode.css`: only `color-scheme` from framework classes / `[data-theme]`). `web-component.ts`
imports `main.css?inline`. **The CSS reads only `--cp-*` and `--base-*`** (2.0 names) — never a
`--pa-*` / `--pc-*`. Sizes are `calc(<n> * var(--cp-rem))`; fallbacks are `light-dark()` pairs.
Never declare a `--base-*` on `:host` (it would shadow the page's theme). Class names stay
`pa-command-palette__*` (the markup is pure-admin's palette markup). `kmwc check-vars --strict`
validates the manifest against the built bundle.

## Invariants that are easy to break

See plan §10. These are the bugs that motivated the project.

- Static vs. dynamic: the `/` and `:` lists and non-`search` steps filter client-side. Only global
  search, context search and `isLiveSearch` steps call providers, debounced (`searchDebounce`).
- A context search with an empty query must NOT call `searchCallback`; show `labels['messages.typeToSearch']`.
  The input keeps a locked `"<shortcut> "` prefix.
- Global search prepends matching commands/contexts (works with no `searchCallback`), then appends
  provider results.
- Keyboard navigation never awaits a provider and must not bump `listVersion`.
- Superseded requests are aborted via `AbortSignal`, and late results are dropped.
- Callback arguments and event details must stay plain JSON, because the LiveView bridge
  serializes them. `searchCallback`/`getStepOptionsCallback` are read live; a provider ctx's
  `signal` (like `controller` / `element`) is attached non-enumerable so `JSON.stringify(ctx)` stays data. `data-search-event` /
  `data-step-options-event` are reserved for the future `../keen-web-commandpalette` bridge.
- The component closes itself after `select` / `action` (unless a before-hook returned `false`), and the host
  performs the effect. Commands first collapse to the one-line feedback (`show-feedback`) (`#showFeedback` in the
  element, `.cp-confirming` hides everything but `.cp-confirm`; the event still fires immediately, `close` follows) — while `#feedbackTimer` is set,
  `#render()` must not repaint over it. The engine reports terminal effects through `host.effect()`, whose answer (`false` = vetoed, a Promise
  = later) decides whether usage is recorded or the wizard steps back to its last answer. Keep-open after a
  successful effect and a reply-directive channel (toast / keep-open) are still future work.
- RTL comes from inherited `direction`: CSS must stay logical (`inset-inline-*`, `margin-inline-*`,
  `inline-size` — no physical left/right), rendered text runs are wrapped in `<bdi>`, and ←/→
  paging swaps via `this.isRTL` (read per keydown, so runtime `dir` flips need no rebuild).
- Icons and strings are data. There is no built-in icon set, and every visible string comes from `labels`.
- Usage entries must stay plain JSON (they're persisted). A run's branch steps are NOT stored: on
  replay, a forking answer is resolved against the step's current options, and Enter's
  fast-forward stops at a step whose list isn't loaded yet rather than guess the branch.
- `Step.getOptionsCallback`, `Context.searchCallback`, `Step.getIsVisibleCallback` and the command
  `get*Callback` / `onClick` are JS-only conveniences; the central `getStepOptionsCallback` /
  `searchCallback` and the `action` event must keep working for server-driven hosts.

## Mirrored in the devkit spotlight

The devkit's example-site chapter search (`../web-components/src/examples/spotlight.js`,
`chapter-search.js`, `css/spotlight.css`) mirrors this component without depending on it: the
shell markup and classes (as `kmwc-spotlight__*`), `matchesAny()` / `highlight()` / `escapeHtml()`,
`bindGlobalKeys()` (core `bindShortcuts` / `isTypingTarget` here; the mirror keeps its own), the input keyboard map, `move()` / `PAGE_STEP`,
`open()` / `close()`, and the dialog / search / results / footer CSS. When you fix a bug in one of
those, port it there too (`../web-components/scripts/spotlight-mirror.json` lists every pair; its
`npm run check:spotlight-mirror` reports what changed here since the last alignment).

**Deliberate differences — open for discussion** (each is marked in the spotlight's code). Decide
per item whether wcp should adopt it, or whether the spotlight should drop it:

- **Rows are links** (`<a href>`), so Ctrl+click and Ctrl/⌘+Enter open a new tab. wcp rows are
  `<div>`s and Ctrl/⌘+Enter means nothing. Worth it for navigation-type commands here?
- **Tab does nothing** in the spotlight (it only keeps focus in the input), because a chapter
  list has no wizard steps. In wcp, Tab selects one wizard step.
- **The section code takes wcp's icon slot** (`__item-code` where wcp renders `__item-icon`), as
  a monospace chip. wcp has no equivalent "short code" field on an item.
- **The search button in the page header is the kit's own** (`kmwc-spotlight__trigger`, a
  🔍 + `Ctrl K` pill). wcp ships no trigger; hosts open it from their own UI.

**Also to discuss — opening the palette makes the page jump sideways** (wcp AND the spotlight).
Both lock scroll with core's `lockBodyScroll()` (`web-components-core` `overlay/scroll-lock.ts`),
which only sets `overflow: hidden` on `<body>`. The page scrollbar disappears and the content
widens by its width — measured on wcp's own example page: 1265 → 1280 px at a 1280 px window
(classic Windows scrollbars; overlay scrollbars hide the problem). The original palette in
`../pure-admin` doesn't jump, for two reasons:

1. **Page CSS:** `html { scrollbar-gutter: stable; }` (pure-admin
   `packages/core/src/scss/core-components/_base.scss`). It must be on `<html>`: Chromium only
   takes the gutter for the viewport from the root element, so on `<body>` it does nothing.
2. **A stronger lock** in pure-css's shared overlay stack (`../pure-css/src/js/pure-css.js`,
   `pa.overlay` `applyLock` / `releaseLock`, used by pure-admin's `command-palette.js` through
   `pureCss.overlay.open(…, { modal: true })`): it pins `<body>` with `position: fixed;
   top: -scrollY` (the only lock iOS Safari honours for touch scrolling) and scrolls back to the
   same place on release. If the scrollbar still disappears (no gutter on `<html>`), it adds the
   lost width back as `padding-inline-end` on `<body>`.

Proposal: bring (2) into core's `lockBodyScroll()` (ref counting stays), so wcp, multiselect's
fullscreen sheet and every other core overlay stop jumping without the host page having to set
(1). Then port it to the spotlight's mirrored copy and move the core `alignedCommit` in
`../web-components/scripts/spotlight-mirror.json`. Tried in the devkit playground:
`scrollbar-gutter: stable` on `<html>` during the lock keeps the layout still (card edge stays
at 1233 px open and closed).

Out of scope here: the keen bridge, Svelte/React/Razor wrappers, the directive-return channel, and migrating the existing palettes.
